clue.text: Fictitious American sailor returning home

indicators.note: a sailor returning goes back the way he came, so his name is read backwards

parts.note: gob is American slang for a sailor in the navy
for an American sailor coming back, home is the US

explanation.surface: A made-up tale about a US navy man coming back to his home port.
explanation.walkthrough: GOB is US slang a non-American may not know; 'home' is the sailor's homeland, the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bogus is fake or sham, as a fictitious story is invented and untrue.

clue.text: Raven's pale such an unusual bird!

definitions.text: Raven's pale such an unusual bird!

parts.words: Raven's pale such an unusual bird!
parts.note: a pale raven would be odd; the rare bird meant is coloured like a raven but shaped like the usual white river bird

explanation.walkthrough: The pale bird is the swan, usually white; one with a raven's colour is proverbially rare.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird was long the stock example of something impossible or extremely rare.

clue.text: "Grow up, dear!" -alternately "Cheese it!"

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the quoted words, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A parent tells a child to mature, then says to stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese it!' is old slang for 'stop it', but only 'Cheese' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild yellow Dutch cheese.

clue.text: Helps gulls, say

indicators.note: say signals the word for gulls is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: gulls as a noun are dupes, easily fooled people

explanation.surface: Somebody aids seabirds.
explanation.definitionFit: To succour is to give aid to someone in need.

clue.text: Deposition from Us lawyer opposing one in a noisy suit

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical marking for loud

indicators.note: the lawyer, the versus and the one sit inside the word for suit

parts.note: to suit is to fit, be right for
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
V is short for versus, against
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sworn evidence taken from an American attorney who is up against someone in a loud legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like a lawsuit but means to fit; 'in' puts the lawyer, versus and one inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposition is sworn written testimony, which is exactly what an affidavit records.

clue.text: In a position to put down island rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: Able to suppress an uprising on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' means write down the island; 'rising' turns ELBA upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to do something means being capable of it.

clue.text: Scores success with kings at nap

parts.note: two scores make forty, a score being twenty
a win is a success
K is king, so two kings are KS

explanation.surface: Someone tallies a victory with high cards at the card game Napoleon.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap is also a card game, which suits the scoring and kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty winks is an idiom for a short sleep.

clue.text: E.g. first four letters reversed in childhood — not for the first time

definitions.text: childhood — not for the first time

indicators.note: reversed applies to everything before it, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. is written as the letters E and G
the first four letters of the alphabet are A to D

explanation.surface: A child learning ABCD, getting them backwards again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns EG plus A TO D into DOTAGE. 'not for the first time' makes it second childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the feeble state of old age, often called a second childhood.

clue.text: Art museum — £1,000 is included for damage

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum of art and design in London

indicators.note: the pound and thousand letters have the word is put between them

parts.note: the pound sign is L and the Roman numeral for a thousand is M

explanation.surface: A gallery takes in a grand to pay for repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Vandalism is wilful destruction of property.

clue.text: Figure said by some to precede the twins

indicators.note: the sign is pronounced this way by some speakers, so it is heard only

parts.note: the zodiac sign before Gemini, the twins, is the bull

explanation.surface: A star sign said to come just before the twins.
explanation.walkthrough: Taurus comes before Gemini in the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is a ring-shaped geometric figure like a doughnut.

clue.text: Such a relatively stern reproof from Dutchman

definitions.text: Such a relatively stern reproof from Dutchman

parts.words: Such a relatively stern reproof from Dutchman
parts.note: a stern lecture from a 'Dutch uncle' is the kind of telling-off a relative, an uncle, might give

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch uncle' is an idiom for someone who lectures you sternly; 'relatively' hints at an uncle, a relation.
explanation.definitionFit: Avuncular means like an uncle, and a frank reproof from a Dutch uncle comes from that kind of family figure.

clue.text: Meaning "voice" of course

explanation.surface: A note that the word for sense also names a singing part, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of a speech is its gist or drift; a tenor is also the high adult male singing voice.

clue.text: King careless on the horn

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
lax means slack or careless

explanation.surface: A heedless monarch leaning on the car's hooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A klaxon is a loud electric warning hooter, as once fitted to cars.

clue.text: Sounds like crooked informer may end up in Guernsey

indicators.note: the clue says the word for crooked is only heard, spelt differently

parts.note: wry means twisted or crooked
a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A bent informer could be shipped off to a Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Guernsey is not the island but a breed of dairy cow, which eats the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryegrass is a pasture grass, so it ends up eaten by a grazing cow of the Guernsey breed.

clue.text: Put clue, say, as anagram of oil-producer"

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is told to write a clue as a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The gum tree yields a pungent medicinal oil from its leaves.

clue.text: Work on Thames much appreciated, by George!

definitions.text: Work on Thames much appreciated, by George!

parts.words: Work on Thames much appreciated, by George!
parts.note: Handel's suite was first played on a barge on the Thames and pleased King George I; 'by George!' also reads as an exclamation

explanation.walkthrough: 'by George!' reads as an oath, but the king who enjoyed the piece was George I.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel wrote this orchestral suite for a royal river trip on the Thames in 1717 for George I.

clue.text: The point about Abram's origin — man of divine power

indicators.note: about means the outer words go round the city

parts.note: the gist is the main point
Abram came from Ur of the Chaldees in Genesis

explanation.surface: A preacher sums up where the patriarch came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A theurgist works miracles through supernatural agency.

clue.text: Current form includes one's record

indicators.note: the form of current holds the other letters within it

parts.note: DC is direct current, one form of electric current
one's is read as 'one is', giving I and S

explanation.surface: A present-day questionnaire contains a person's personal history.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, the vinyl kind.

clue.text: Agreement on point in the enumeration

indicators.note: the word on and the point go inside the count

parts.note: a census is an official count of the population
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Accord reached on one item in the head count.
explanation.definitionFit: Consensus means general accord shared by a group.

clue.text: Libertine inclination he will display

parts.note: rake is the slope or inclination of a stage or mast
he will is contracted to he'll

explanation.surface: A man inclined to vice will reveal himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A rakehell is an old word for a dissolute rogue.

clue.text: He gets maybe one pound for Christmas

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A man is handed a pound as a festive present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' nods to Noel as a man's name; 'maybe' rearranges ONE, which gets the pound after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is an old word for the Yuletide festival, as in carols.

clue.text: Rasher, perhaps, after second game?

indicators.note: the bacon cut comes after the word for second

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a rasher may be a slice of gammon, cured ham from the hind leg

explanation.surface: Bacon slice offered after a second helping in a quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Briton in Mexico to call in. Japanese game

indicators.note: the second in places the call inside the board game

parts.note: go is a Japanese board game played with stones
to ring is to telephone

explanation.surface: A Briton visiting Mexico phones to arrange a Japanese board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Gringo is Latin American slang for a foreigner from an English-speaking country.

clue.text: Paints fish by the seaside

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two words sit side by side

parts.note: a port is a town on the seaside coast
rays are flat fish such as skates

explanation.surface: An artist depicts fish down at the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to depict them, as an artist paints a picture.

clue.text: Fruit pronounced sound

indicators.note: pronounced means the fruit is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit

explanation.surface: A fruit declared to be healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb the sea is to measure its depth, as a sailor does with a lead line.

clue.text: Implore a person to make himself scarce

parts.note: to implore is to beg
one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: Pleading with somebody to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old command meaning go away, ordering someone to vanish.

clue.text: Rosie found indisposed in bed

indicators.note: indisposed means unwell or out of order, so the name is rearranged

explanation.surface: Rosie was found ill and lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is an osier bed, where willows are grown.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiers are willows grown in osier beds for basket-making.

clue.text: With which Moss is said to be a fly-by-night

definitions.text: With which Moss is said to be a fly-by-night

parts.words: With which Moss is said to be a fly-by-night
parts.note: said with this speech defect, the S in Moss comes out as TH, turning the plant into a night-flying insect

explanation.definitionFit: A lithp, a speech impediment, turns S into TH, so the name comes out as a night-flying insect.

clue.text: Workhouse wedding

explanation.definitionFit: A union was a group of parishes running a Victorian poorhouse, also called the union; a union is also a marriage.

clue.text: One result that is altered in Old Palace Gardens

indicators.note: altered means these letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single outcome is changed at a historic royal park.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuileries are Paris gardens on the site of the vanished royal palace of that name.

clue.text: Weaver's leading the call to drain our bumpers

definitions.text: the call to drain our bumpers

explanation.definitionFit: Nick Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so Bottom's up has him on top; and it is a drinking toast for draining full glasses.

clue.text: Sailor I saw holding monkey like creature

indicators.note: the three words hold the creature's name within them

explanation.surface: A seaman reports spotting an ape-like animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A loris is a slow-moving nocturnal primate of Asia, resembling a small monkey.
